title: Tiered response policy sketch
body:
Context / motivation:
- We need a simple, composable way for apps to express response "tiers" (high-fidelity, balanced, cheap-fast) that map to model+config selection and fallback sequences.
- Goal: give product engineers easy knobs to trade latency/cost/quality per request (or per customer segment) without adding bespoke routing logic.
- Should integrate with existing smart routing & fallback stack (region/capacity/quantized variants).

High-level idea:
- Define a lightweight Tiered Response Policy (TRP) DSL that maps logical tiers to lists of candidate model+config variants plus routing rules and cost/latency guards.
- Runtime evaluates policy per request with context (customer tier, latency SLO, cost budget, feature flags) and returns the chosen variant.
- If chosen variant fails (lack of capacity, timeout, unacceptable output), fall back to next candidate or apply a degrade strategy (abbreviated response / cached answer / error).

PRD-ish outline (rough):
- Name: Tiered Response Policy (sketch)
- Who: platform APIs + product teams embedding LLMs in UX (search, assistants, summaries)
- What: policy object + admin UI + simple SDK helper to attach policy to route or API key
- Why: reduce per-team engineering cost of building cost-aware fallbacks, speed up canaries and staged rollouts, protect latency-sensitive flows

Core components:
1) Policy DSL (JSON/YAML) - minimal fields:
   - tiers: ordered list (e.g., ["premium", "standard", "economy"])
   - for each tier: candidates: ordered list of {model, variant, quant, max_tokens, batch_hint}
   - guards: optional thresholds (max_latency_ms, max_cost_per_req_usd, min_quality_score)
   - signals: which runtime signals to consider (latency_estimate, capacity_level, recent_regression_flag)
   - fallback_behavior: choices = [next_candidate, use_cached, shorten_response, fail_fast]

   Example snippet:
   {
     "tiers": [
       {"name":"premium", "candidates":[{"model":"rw-large-v1","quant":"fp16"}]},
       {"name":"standard","candidates":[{"model":"rw-medium-v2","quant":"int8"},{"model":"rw-medium-v2-quant","quant":"int4"}]},
       {"name":"economy","candidates":[{"model":"rw-small-v1","quant":"int4"}]}
     ],
     "guards": {"max_latency_ms":120, "max_cost_per_req_usd":0.003}
   }

2) Evaluation runtime hooks:
   - before dispatch: evaluate policy with current signals (latency SLO for route, customer budget, region capacity)
   - select first candidate that meets guards when estimated token cost + latency <= thresholds
   - if none meet guards: either choose cheapest and mark as degraded or return a controlled error per fallback_behavior

3) Telemetry + observability:
   - per-policy metrics: chosen-tier distribution, average cost, P95 latency, fallback rate, quality regression alerts (linked to evals)
   - event logs capturing why a candidate was skipped (capacity, guard fail, circuit open)

User stories (quick):
- As a mobile app PM, I want summary API calls for free users to use the economy tier so average cost per request stays under $0.002, and premium users to get high-fidelity model with 99th pct latency < 150ms.
- As an infra engineer, I want a policy that automatically falls back from dedicated pool -> shared-hosted pool when dedicated is saturated, without changing client code.
- As a platform engineer, I want to test a new quantized variant by adding it to the middle of the standard tier candidates (A/B by ranking) and monitor quality/regressions for 2 weeks before promoting.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Basic JSON policy format supported by API backend and SDK flag to attach policy to a route or key
- Runtime picks candidate, applies guards, logs decision reasons, and performs fallback to next candidate on capacity errors
- Dashboard: per-policy view with tier selection distribution, cost, latency, fallback rate (last 7d)
- Simple CLI to validate policy syntax and simulate decisions with stubbed signals

Phases / rollout plan:
- Phase 0: internal-only experiment for 2 product teams (search and inbox summarization) — iterate on DSL and telemetry
- Phase 1: beta self-serve in Console for selected customers, add guard knobs in UI (latency & cost caps)
- Phase 2: GA with templates (e.g., "cost-first", "latency-first", "quality-first") and policy export/import

Metrics to watch:
- Mean cost per request by policy and by customer segment
- P50/P90/P95 latency by tier and chosen candidate
- Fallback rate and root causes (capacity vs guard violation vs timeout)
- Quality regressions (evals fail) after new candidate promotions

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Start with server-side evaluation only; keep SDK simple (policy id or attach inline)
- Use existing capacity signals + cost estimator (token-based) from Optimize service
- Avoid complex on-call semantics in MVP (circuit breakers can be added later)
- Need to ensure logging includes non-PII request hash and policy id for triage

Experiments and safety checks:
- Canary quantized variants behind a quality gate: don't promote if eval score drops > 2% on a prompt set
- Soft-fallback rollouts: route 95% to primary candidate, 5% to new candidate, track drift in latency & quality

Open questions / tradeoffs (TODO):
- How aggressive should guards be defaulted for new policies? Conservative (prefer quality) or aggressive (cost savings)?
- Where do we store policies? DB table per org or generic policy catalog with owner? Access control model?
- UX for composing policies: advanced DSL vs templated UI plus editable JSON?
- Interaction with dedicated capacity billing — if policy routes to shared-hosted fallback, how to bill and surface to customers?

Next actions (short list):
- Sync with Lina & Omar next Tue to align on DSL minimal fields and telemetry events list
- Prototype policy evaluator (library) that takes signals and returns candidate id (1 week spike)
- Create Confluence stub for internal policy catalog and RBAC notes

Notes to self (random ideas):
- Consider a "grace budget" token that allows occasional higher-cost choices for premium sessions (preserve UX for key user journeys).
- Could expose a per-request inline hint (max_cost_usd or prefer_latency) to override policy in emergencies.
- When in doubt, default to "shorten_response" rather than full failure for UX flows that tolerate partial answers.

-- end of sketch --

(rough, informal. will flesh out DSL examples and UX screenshots after the spike.)
